VibePascal v54 -- aarch64-linux native compiler (runs on ARM64 Linux, e.g. Raspberry Pi 64-bit)
Source commit: b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e
Compiler fix:  b9cb8fea875670cfc48f7d83b88d4af39a28aa6e
Parent release: v53 (9e20efe4d6912fe6a9558c442ae4fa8d5dfe3045)
Built: 2026-09-03 on x86_64-linux
Binary: bin/ppca64  md5 5cc202e1ee758321f9fba15aa7fb8ba8

Change: an untyped INTEGER initialiser for an inline var (and for an inferred
`for var i := ...` counter) now infers NativeInt instead of the hard-coded
LongInt -- pointer width, so 8 bytes on a 64-bit target and 4 on a 32-bit one.
A string/char literal initialiser now infers exactly what a bare `string`
denotes at that point (wide under -Mdelphiunicode/-Munleashed; ShortString
under $H-, which earlier releases got wrong).  Only types narrower than
NativeInt are widened, so Int64/QWord keep their width; explicit typecasts
such as byte(10) are never promoted.

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Nothing in the RTL, the packages or the PPU format
changed between v53 and v54, so an existing unit set for this platform stays
valid.  Full change + validation record: dist/win64/staging-v54/VERSION.txt.

RUNTIME VERIFIED UNDER EMULATION (2026-09-10, corrects the original v54 text).
The original note here said this binary "has never been executed".  That is no
longer true.  qemu-user-static was not installed on the build host; it is a
stock Ubuntu package and installing it was one command.  Measured:

  - bin/ppca64 RUNS on aarch64.  `ppca64 -iV` -> 3.3.1, exit 0.  Statically
    linked, so no aarch64 sysroot is needed to start it.
  - It COMPILES and its output RUNS.  Against rtl/units/aarch64-linux from the
    same source commit (host cross binutils via -XPaarch64-linux-gnu-), the
    emulated ppca64 built tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp and the resulting
    aarch64 executable ran: checks=45 fails=0, NativeInt=8, VERDICT:PASS.
  - The full cy1096 block-scope finalization matrix (330 lines, 22 control-flow
    corners) also compiled and ran here: MATRIX PASS, every corner released
    exactly once.

Together with the arm-linux result (NativeInt=4 on 32-bit ARM) this is the
first execution proof of BOTH halves of directive mtkt2shb on real ARM
instruction sets: pointer-width on a 64-bit target, 32-bit on a 32-bit target.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: qemu-user is an emulator, not aarch64 hardware.  It runs the
real shipped bytes and real aarch64 encodings, so codegen and RTL defects show
up -- but it is not a sign-off on physical silicon, and nobody has run these
artifacts on an actual aarch64 machine yet.

REPRODUCE IT YOURSELF: dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh re-runs every claim above from
a clean checkout (installs nothing; it tells you which two packages it needs).
It hash-checks each shipped compiler against the md5 in its own VERSION.txt and
refuses to continue on a mismatch, so a pass is a statement about the published
bytes, not about a local rebuild.
